Subject: Converting to annual prepay — possible concessions and timing

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran numbers with the Ops and Finance teams and are seriously considering switching our Redwood usage from monthly pay-as-you-go to an annual prepay commitment for 2026.

Primary asks from our side:
- Outline of term discounts for 1yr vs 2yr vs 3yr prepay (list % by year).
- Suggested ramp schedule — we expect tokens to grow ~2.5x over next 12 months but need a staged prepay schedule.
- Any one-time credits or onboarding concessions for moving from monthly billing mid-quarter.
- Procurement timeline: what paperwork (SOW/Order Form/DocuSign) and typical lead times for finance sign-off?

We can share the RFP workbook if helpful (I attached a stub below). Also looping Amelia from our procurement partner to help coordinate required docs.

Appreciate a rough proposal and whether an early-signing credit is available.

Best,

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 10:05:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting to annual prepay — possible concessions and timing

Francisco — thanks for the clear asks. Happy to own distance coordination and get you a concise proposal. High-level answers up front:

- Term discounts: we typically tier discounts by committed spend and term length. Ballpark: 10% for 1yr at similar commit, 15% for 2yr, 20% for 3yr — exacts depend on annual spend and whether you want a fixed per-token price or a consumption bucket.
- Ramp schedule: can do staged prepay (quarterly tranches) or an initial partial prepay + top-up model. For customers scaling quickly, we recommend a 30/30/40 split across first three quarters to avoid overpaying upfront.
- One-time credits: we can offer a mid-cycle conversion credit (applied to first invoice) to offset prorated overlap — scope depends on commitment size; will confirm with finance.
- Procurement: we use an Order Form + Master Services Agreement (standard). DocuSign turnaround typically 2–5 business days after legal review; PO-friendly invoicing available.

Marissa — can you draft a term sheet with two concession scenarios (aggressive vs standard) and include suggested ramp tables? Ben — please indicate what credit buckets we can offer for mid-cycle conversions and any constraints on recognized revenue for 2/3-year deals.

Francisco — I'll get a formal PDF term sheet to you by Monday. If you prefer a short call to walk the execs through the trade-offs, we can schedule early next week.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 14:20:37 -07:00
Subject: Term sheet (draft) + ramp options attached

Francisco, Dylan — attaching a draft term sheet and two ramp schedules. I pulled the numbers off your RFP workbook and created three commitment scenarios:

1) Conservative (1yr, smaller commit) — 10% term discount, no early-signing credit, quarterly prepay allowed
2) Growth (2yr, staged prepay) — 15% term discount, one-time conversion credit equal to 2% of first-year committed spend, recommended 30/30/40 ramp
3) Aggressive (3yr, fixed price bucket) — 20% term discount, early-signing credit 3% if signed within 14 days, balanced annual top-up option

Notes / open items:
- We can accept mid-quarter conversion, but the credit depends on total committed ARR (Ben, see note).
- If you want committed per-token rates rather than unit pricing buckets, we need a definitive usage baseline for revenue recognition.
- SLA and data retention add-ons are billable; let us know if Nimbus needs SOC 2 evidence or additional controls.

Attachment: redwood-multi-year-term-sheet.pdf

Next steps suggested:
- Francisco to confirm which scenario (Conservative/Growth/Aggressive) your finance prefers.
- If Growth/Aggressive, legal will insert a tailored Order Form; expect 3–7 business days.
- We'll prepare a mutual action plan with milestones for finance approvals and signature.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the schedules.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Francisco — attaching a short MAP and a consolidated overage table for the Growth scenario. Key points: 

- Growth scenario (15%): we recommend committing to an initial bucket aligned to your Q2 forecast with a scheduled top-up at the start of Q3 and Q4 (30/30/40). The overage rate is 1.8x the committed per-token price; we included examples at 20%, 50%, and 100% over baseline.
- Conversion credit: we can make the 2% conversion credit explicit on the first invoice. It is applied after invoice generation (credit memo).
- Early-signing credit (3% for 3yr): not combinable with marketplace referral credits; only one promotional credit applies.
- Revenue recognition: for multi-year fixed-price buckets, we amortize revenue per ASC rules; no special revenue holds beyond normal renewals.
- DocuSign: I created an Order Form draft with placeholders for bucket amounts. Link: https://www.docusign.com/exec/nbh-045 (sample).

Attachments included in this message: redwood-multi-year-term-sheet.pdf (updated), MAP_NBH-045.pdf (mutual action plan), Overages_GrowthScenario.csv (table).

If Nimbus is comfortable with the Growth scenario, we recommend scheduling an internal approval call with your CFO this week. Once we have sign-off, we can finalize the Order Form and push to DocuSign — typical signature timeline 48–72 hours.

Ben Carter
